# Lighting upgrades and relay harnesses

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Install Hella Optilux bulbs using a main power line, three Pico waterproof relays, and various wire gauges. [t760]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Strip the ends of a 15-foot pack of 12-gauge Noble brand wire.
2. [Partial] Connect one end of that main power line to a copper 2-gauge compression connector using ring terminals on both sides.
3. [Partial] Attach the other end of the main power line to an in-line fuse holder with a 40-amp Pico waterproof relay inside it.
4. [Partial] Run about 6 inches of 10-gauge wire from one side of that first splitter to connect to another in-line fuse holder containing a second identical relay.
5. [Partial] Connect the remaining output of the first splitter (the other short 10-gauge wire) to an additional in-line fuse holder with its own Pico waterproof relay inside it.
6. [Partial] Attach two 9007 male sockets, each fitted with 12-gauge pigtails, to the outputs of the low beam and high beam relays respectively using butt splices.
7. Connect a braided wire sleeve over the main power line where it meets the splitter for protection.
8. [Partial] Install Hella Optilux 85/100 watt bulbs into the two male sockets you just connected.
9. Secure all connections with various shrink wrap tubes to insulate them from moisture and heat.
10. [Partial] Wrap any remaining exposed wires or joints with a roll of rubber splicing tape.

_Procedure reported by [t760]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-build-relay-harness-for-100-watt-headlight-bulbs.8850/>_
